assumptions.condition: For distinct \(i,j\in[n]\), \(B^{(0)}_{ij}\ne0\) if and only if \(j\to i\) is an edge of \(\mathcal G\).

standard.name: one stochastic perfect intervention per latent node

assumptions.condition: For every \(m\in\mathcal E\), the spectrum of the fixed-coordinate covariance \(\Sigma_m\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) lies in \([\kappa^{-1},\kappa]\).

standard.name: uniform covariance conditioning on the observation support

assumptions.condition: Every eigenvalue of every matrix occurrence \(R(M)\) in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\), including each singleton encoder query, belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)\).

novel.justification: This is a pre-sampling model promise on a named public computation path. It is realized with constant \(g_0\) by the uniformly conditioned bipartite family in Theorem 2 even though an unqueried subset is exponentially ill separated.

assumptions.condition: Every graph-loop comparison \(c_{t,j}(P)\) in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\) belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[h_0,1]\).

novel.justification: The condition is stated on actual projector geometry and is checkable from the declared population model. Coordinate-range intervention systems, including the separation family, have comparisons exactly zero or one.

assumptions.condition: Conditional on the fixed environment labels, observations are independent within and across environments and have their corresponding laws under \(P\).

definitions.name: Gaussian primitive score-correlation family
definitions.construction: Fix the canonical coordinates \(U\) on \(\mathcal S\). For every \(m\in[n]\), compute \(\Theta_m=\Sigma_m^{-1}\) and \(\Delta_m=\Theta_0-\Theta_m\). Gaussian score algebra on the induced law \(P_m\) gives \(s_m(y)=-\Theta_my\), \(d_m(y)=\Delta_my\), and \(R_m=\mathbb E_{P_0}[d_m(Y^{(0)})d_m(Y^{(0)})^{\top}]=\Delta_m\Sigma_0\Delta_m\); for \(M\subseteq[n]\), set \(R(M)=\sum_{m\in M}R_m\).

definitions.name: public population program \(\mathsf A\)
definitions.construction: Starting from the observed intervention-label set \(V=[n]\) with \(|V|=t\), inspect \(R(V\setminus\{k\})\) for every remaining label and remove the smallest label \(k\) whose queried matrix has rank \(t-1\). Reverse the removal order to obtain \(\pi\). In decreasing order index and increasing later index, compare \(\|P_{\operatorname{col}}(R(V_t))P_{\operatorname{null}}(R(M_{t,j}))\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), where \(M_{t,j}=V_j\setminus(\{\pi_t\}\cup D_t)\) and \(D_t\) is the descendant-closed set already recorded for \(\pi_t\); add the corresponding arrow between observed intervention labels exactly when the comparison is zero, preserve recorded arrows, and query every singleton \(R_m\) for the row \(m\) of the environment-labelled encoder class.

definitions.name: executed transcript \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\)
definitions.construction: The ordered multiset of all matrix occurrences and projector-product comparisons evaluated when \(\mathsf A\) is run at exact population input \(P\), with duplicate subsets retained as separate occurrences.

definitions.name: promised transcript-local class \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\)
definitions.construction: \(\{P=(P_m:m\in\mathcal E): n\ge2,\ P\text{ satisfies the linear Gaussian DAG equations, one perfect variance-reset intervention per target, injective mixing, observed conditioning, reached eigen band, reached projector band, and independent environment sampling}\}\).

definitions.name: terminal sample budget
definitions.construction: Set \(e_{\star}=\min\{g_0h_0/(16n),\tau g_0/(4\sqrt n)\}\), \(b_{\star}=\min\{(2\kappa)^{-1},e_{\star}/(40\kappa^4)\}\), \(q_{\star}=64\kappa^2/b_{\star}^2\), \(t_0=n\log 9+\log(2(n+1)/\alpha)\), and \(u_{\star}=t_0+\log(16q_{\star})\). Let \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}=2^{\lceil\log_2(\max\{n,\lceil32q_{\star}u_{\star}^2\rceil\})\rceil}\) be the cumulative post-support cap in every environment. The observational environment uses at most \(B_0=n+B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) observations after including its disjoint \(n\)-observation support batch, every intervention environment uses at most \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\), and the total across all environments is at most \(B_{\mathrm{tot}}=n+(n+1)B_{\mathrm{samp}}\).

definitions.name: recover-or-abstain certificate \(\mathsf C\)
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sup}}\), the disjoint \(n\)-draw observational support batch, to recover its span; if that span has dimension below \(n\), return \(\bot\) without inversion. On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}}\), the span equals the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\), so apply the public canonical-frame rule to obtain exactly \(U\) and set \(Y_i^{(m)}=U^{\top}X_i^{(m)}\). Maintain one retained post-support stream in each environment. At stage \(r=0\), retain the first \(N_0=1\) observation from each stream; at every stage \(r\ge1\), append exactly \(N_r-N_{r-1}\) new observations, so the cumulative stream contains exactly \(N_r=2^r\) observations per environment. For \(r<r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\), sample and retain observations only; do not form an inverse or run any spectral or projector test. For \(r\ge r_0\), assign error \(\alpha\,2^{-r-1}\), form each \(S_{m,r}=N_r^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N_r}Y_i^{(m)}Y_i^{(m)\top}\) from the same retained prefix, invert it in \(\mathbb R^n\), and compute \(\widehat R_{m,r}=(S_{0,r}^{-1}-S_{m,r}^{-1})S_{0,r}(S_{0,r}^{-1}-S_{m,r}^{-1})\). Enclose each primitive matrix within operator radius \(e_r=40\kappa^4a_r\). Restart \(\mathsf A\) from its initial state and accept a rank only when every Weyl interval selects exactly one of \(\{0\}\) and \([g_0,\infty)\); accept a projector comparison only when its propagated interval selects exactly one of \(\{0\}\) and \([h_0,1]\). Use the smallest certified-zero observed intervention label. Return the graph on those labels and, for each singleton range, map a certified coordinate unit vector \(v_m\in\operatorname{col}(R_m)\) to the ambient encoder row \(v_m^{\top}U^{\top}\); return only after the entire transcript is resolved. Otherwise report \(\bot\), retain all samples, and advance to the next doubling stage.

definitions.name: parent-range encoder loss
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)=\inf\{\|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}: \|H^{\star}_{m,:}\|_2=1,\ H^{\star}_{m,:}{}^{\top}\in\mathcal S,\ U^{\top}H^{\star}_{m,:}{}^{\top}\in\operatorname{col}(R_m)\text{ for every }m\in[n],\ (H^{\star}G)_{m,I(j)}=0\text{ whenever }j\ne m\text{ and }j\not\to m\text{ in }\mathcal G_{\mathcal E}\}\).

definitions.name: published threshold scales and valid projector lower bound
definitions.construction: After the isometric reduction to fixed support coordinates, Acartürk et al.'s Section 5 equation (22) is \(\eta^{\ast}(P)=\min\{\lambda_i(R(M)):M\subseteq[n],\ i\in[n],\ \lambda_i(R(M))>0\}\). Their printed equation (23) is \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_{i\in[n]}\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). Separately, the valid projector geometry is quantified by \(\rho_i(G)=(\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2)^{-1}\) and \(\rho^{\ast}(G)=\min_{i\in[n]}\rho_i(G)\); \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\) is not the printed \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)\).

definitions.name: Gaussian bipartite witness \(\mathfrak F_n\)
definitions.construction: For each \(n\ge4\), let \(G=I_n\), let independent \(E_i\sim N(0,1)\) satisfy \(Z_1=E_1\), \(Z_2=E_2\), \(Z_3=Z_1+Z_2+E_3\), \(Z_4=Z_1+(1+2^{-n})Z_2+E_4\), and \(Z_j=E_j\) for \(j\ge5\). In intervention \(i\), replace the equation for \(Z_i\) by an independent \(N(0,2)\) draw and leave all other mechanisms fixed.

definitions.name: certified rational spectral handle \(\mathsf C_{\mathbb Q}\)
definitions.construction: Compose outward-rounded rational covariance and inverse enclosures with a deterministic Hermitian gap and invariant-subspace routine, then bound projector-product norms by interval matrix multiplication and certified singular-value enclosures. Allocate arithmetic error at each reached operation from the unused fraction of the public statistical tolerance and increase \(p_{\mathrm{bit}}\) until every interval is separated from the decision boundary.

statements.statement: For every stage \(r\ge r_0\), if \(\max_{m\in\mathcal E}\|S_{m,r}-\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le a_r\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\), then every \(S_{m,r}\) is invertible as an \(n\times n\) matrix and \(\max_{m\in[n]}\|\widehat R_{m,r}-R_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le40\kappa^4a_r=e_r\). Consequently, simultaneously for every \(M\subseteq[n]\), \(\|\widehat R_r(M)-R(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le |M|e_r\).
statements.justification: This is the deterministic bridge from observable covariance confidence balls to every spectral decision used by the certificate.
statements.gap: Acartürk et al. control estimated score correlations; the Gaussian specialization here must include covariance inversion and a fully empirical primitive matrix.
statements.consumer: It provides the error budget used by interval ranks, projectors, and encoder bars in the official finite-sample implementation.

statements.statement: For any \(S,T\subseteq[n]\), all projectors below act on the fixed space \(\mathbb R^n\), and \[\left\|P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in T\}}P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in S\}^{\perp}}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T\subseteq S.\] For every witness label \(i\in T\setminus S\), the left-hand side is at least \(\rho_i(G)=1/(\|A^{-\top}e_i\|_2\|Ae_i\|_2)=1/(\|H^{\top}e_i\|_2\|Ge_i\|_2)>0\), and hence at least \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\). The source's printed quantity \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\) is a norm product, not this reciprocal lower bound.
statements.justification: The graph transcript needs a correct zero-versus-positive projector characterization under nonorthogonal mixing.
statements.gap: The printed norm-product expression in the closest source can exceed one and a subset-pseudoinverse identity used with it is false; this proposition uses dual vectors and actual projector geometry.
statements.consumer: It prevents false edge decisions in the population proof and supplies the geometric quantity to be enclosed numerically.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\), the support batch satisfies \(\Pr_P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}})=1\). On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}}\), the procedure recovers the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\) and its canonical frame \(U\) exactly, samples without inversion for \(r<r_0\), and begins covariance inversion and all spectral and projector tests in \(\mathbb R^n\) only at \(r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\). Moreover, \[\Pr_P\!\left(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}},\ \widehat{\mathcal G}=\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E})=I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I,\ \mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)\le\tau,\ \text{and return occurs by }B_{\mathrm{samp}}\text{ cumulative post-support samples per environment}\right)\ge1-\alpha.\] On this event the observational environment uses at most \(B_0=n+B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) observations including the disjoint support batch, every intervention environment uses at most \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\), and the combined budget is at most \(B_{\mathrm{tot}}=n+(n+1)B_{\mathrm{samp}}\). At any certified stage \(r\ge r_0\) with primitive radius \(e_r\), there exists \(H^{\star}\) with \(H^{\star}_{m,:}{}^{\top}\in\mathcal S\), \(\|H^{\star}_{m,:}\|_2=1\), and \(U^{\top}H^{\star}_{m,:}{}^{\top}\in\operatorname{col}(R_m)\) for every \(m\), such that \(\|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm F}\le4\sqrt n\,e_r/g_0\), and \((H^{\star}G)_{m,I(j)}=0\) whenever \(j\ne m\) and \(j\not\to m\) in \(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E}\). No eigenvalue margin for a subset absent from \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\) appears in the guarantee.
statements.justification: It is the positive kernel of the query-local beta-min boundary and yields a permutation-equivariant recover-or-abstain guarantee.
statements.gap: Acartürk et al. require the global all-subset \(\eta^{\ast}\) condition together with the separate printed \(\gamma^{\ast}\) threshold condition and do not give an anytime-valid abstention contract or a covariance-specialized encoder range bar.
statements.consumer: The official finite-sample linear CRL package can expose public gaps, certified ties, graph abstention, and encoder error bars.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge4\), the explicit model \(\mathfrak F_n\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32)\). Every fixed-coordinate covariance has spectrum in \([1/32,32]\); the transcript \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\) has exactly \(n^2+2n-2\) matrix occurrences; every reached positive eigenvalue is at least \(1/40\); every reached graph comparison is zero or one; and both the printed source scale and the valid reciprocal scale satisfy \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\). The source thresholds obey \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), whereas its rank-threshold premise fails because \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) and the subset \(\{3,4\}\) is not reached but \[\eta^{\ast}(P)\le\lambda_{\min}^{+}(R(\{3,4\}))\le2^{-2n-1}<1/80.\] The family also satisfies every non-margin condition of Acartürk et al.'s graph theorem: the induced support-coordinate densities and causal conditionals are strictly positive and continuously differentiable, there is one distinct single-target intervention per node, their Assumption 1 parent-ratio condition holds, and the empirical Gaussian covariance score-difference estimator satisfies their consistency condition (15).
statements.justification: This proves that the local promise is a strict geometric relaxation rather than a cosmetic rewrite of the published margin.
statements.gap: Acartürk et al.'s all-subset analysis provides no legal, uniformly conditioned all-dimension family separating off-path from reached spectral geometry.
statements.consumer: It gives a regression fixture for testing that implementation complexity and sample warnings depend on executed queries rather than exponentially bad unused subsets.

statements.statement: Consider the linear Gaussian perfect-intervention subclass satisfying the common non-margin hypotheses of Acartürk et al.'s graph theorem and the observed-conditioning bound \(\kappa\). Section 5 of that source selects \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\), where equation (22) defines the all-subset positive-eigenvalue minimum, and independently selects \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), where printed equation (23) defines \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). Fix \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=g_0/2\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=h_0/2\). On the common actual-geometry subregion satisfying the reached projector band \(c_{t,j}(P)\in\{0\}\cup[h_0,1]\), the complete fixed-margin source premise \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\ge g_0\), \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\), and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), together with strictly positive continuously differentiable support-coordinate densities and causal conditionals, one distinct single-target intervention per node, Assumption 1's parent-ratio condition, and score-difference consistency (15), implies the two transcript-local bands: equation (22) bounds every reached positive eigenvalue below by \(g_0\), and the common actual-geometry restriction supplies the reached projector band. Proposition 1 separately certifies that each nonzero comparison witnessed by label \(i\) is at least \(\rho_i(G)\). Therefore this fixed-margin source region restricted by the common reached projector band is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\). The inclusion is strict at \((g_0,h_0,\kappa)=(1/40,1/2,32)\) for every \(n\ge4\): \(\mathfrak F_n\) satisfies all listed non-margin source conditions, every reached comparison is zero or one, \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\in(0,1)\), but it lies outside the source region because \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1}<\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\), while Theorem 1 certifies it from the reached bands. No containment of the uncorrected published premise in the transcript-local class is asserted, because a lower bound on the printed norm product \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)\) does not imply a lower bound on the reciprocal projector scale \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\) or on the actual comparisons.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates the strict relaxation of the source's all-subset spectral premise while keeping its printed threshold condition and the actual projector geometry distinct.
statements.gap: Acartürk et al.'s Lemma 13 controls ranks for every subset through the global minimum; no checked source proves that the executed program admits a strictly larger constant-gap class.
statements.consumer: Users can certify easy executions that fail the source's global rank-threshold premise while exposing the separate actual projector gap used by the implementation.

statements.statement: If every covariance and spectral enclosure in \(\mathsf C\) is replaced by its zero-radius population singleton, then \(\mathsf C\) makes exactly the same smallest-label order, environment-labelled graph, and environment-indexed singleton-range decisions as \(\mathsf A\), and its graph output is \(\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E})=I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\).
statements.justification: This is the required standard-case reduction from the sequential certificate to the known exact population recovery map.
statements.gap: The source population algorithm uses exact ranks and orthogonality; the new certificate must reduce to those decisions rather than define a different target.
statements.consumer: It gives a deterministic oracle test for the certified implementation and isolates statistical errors from population-logic errors.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf C_{\mathbb Q}\) be realized so that, for rational covariance enclosures of input length \(L\), every rank, repeated-eigenspace, and projector-product decision of \(\mathsf C\) is certified with \(p_{\mathrm{bit}}\le\operatorname{poly}(L,n,\log\kappa,\log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau))\), total Boolean running time polynomial in the same quantities, and total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\)? The construction must terminate on every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\) and preserve Theorem 1's graph and encoder guarantees.
statements.justification: This is the genuinely unresolved bridge from exact-real statistical certification to an executable finite-precision theorem.
statements.gap: Corollary 4.5 of Sobczyk's April 27, 2025 arXiv full version, version 2, gives a certified Hermitian-definite spectral-projector primitive, and Dey et al. give bit-growth templates, but neither source budgets composed forward error for an adaptive CRL transcript with projector-product zero tests.
statements.consumer: Its resolution would make the certificate suitable for the official implementation with machine-checkable rounding guarantees rather than heuristic floating-point thresholds.

sampling_model.design: A preliminary \(n\)-draw observational support batch is disjoint from the covariance streams and spans the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\) with probability one. Its span determines the canonical frame \(U\). Each environment then supplies one retained post-support stream; stage \(r\) uses exactly its first \(N_r=2^r\) coordinate observations \(Y_i^{(m)}=U^{\top}X_i^{(m)}\), so after stage zero only \(N_r-N_{r-1}\) new observations are appended. Stages before \(r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) sample only. At each \(r\ge r_0\), error \(\alpha\,2^{-r-1}\) is spent and the public transcript is restarted using the cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical covariances.
sampling_model.units: Independent centered Gaussian observations in each of the \(n+1\) environments, represented in fixed \(n\)-dimensional coordinates on the deterministic common support \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{col}(G)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(m\in[n]\) is one unknown-target stochastic perfect variance reset; environment \(0\) is observational.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used; the relevant regularity is observed-covariance conditioning by \(\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(r\ge r_0\), cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical second moments from exactly \(N_r\) retained coordinate observations are inverted and mapped exactly to Gaussian score-correlation matrices under the induced laws \(P_m\); no inverse is attempted earlier and no learned score nuisance is required.

estimand_functional: \(\mathsf C(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sup}},\{X_i^{(m)}:m\in\mathcal E,\ i\le N_r\})=(\widehat{\mathcal G},\widehat H)\in\{(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I,\widetilde H):\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widetilde H,P)\le\tau\}\cup\{\bot\},\quad r\ge r_0\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 5 and Theorem 1 select \(\eta\in(0,\eta^{\ast})\) with equation (22)'s all-subset eigenvalue minimum and \(\gamma\in(0,\gamma^{\ast})\) with equation (23)'s printed minimum norm product, under Assumption 1 and score-difference consistency.
For all non-empty subsets of intervention indices, Lemma 4.3 gives a uniform eigenvalue perturbation bound.
Our work develops confidence sequences whose widths go to zero, with nonasymptotic coverage guarantees under nonparametric conditions.
A single intervention on each latent variable is sufficient for identifiability.
Corollary 4.5 computes an approximate spectral projector within prescribed operator-norm error.

tldr: A fixed public rank-and-projector transcript, rather than all exponentially many subset sums, determines the finite-sample difficulty of the Acartürk et al. interventional causal representation learner. In fixed \(n\)-dimensional coordinates on the deterministic observation support, an anytime-valid Gaussian certificate retains one cumulative sample stream per environment, postpones every inverse until \(N_r\ge n\), and returns the transitive closure in observed intervention labels, \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\), together with an encoder whose rows use the same labels, or abstains. An all-dimension Gaussian bipartite family satisfies the source's printed equation (23) threshold condition, has valid reciprocal projector scale \(\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), and meets all non-margin side conditions while keeping reached gaps constant and making equation (22)'s all-subset margin exponentially small. The remaining open content is an end-to-end polynomial-bit rational implementation of every spectral decision.

project_justification.gap: Acartürk et al.'s finite-sample graph-recovery premise combines equation (22)'s global all-subset margin \(\eta^{\ast}\), equation (23)'s printed norm-product scale \(\gamma^{\ast}\), Assumption 1, smooth full-support models, distinct interventions, and consistent score estimation. Its rank analysis still pays for every subset although the deterministic program executes only a polynomial transcript, and its printed norm product must not be identified with the reciprocal lower bound furnished by actual projector geometry.
project_justification.niche: A public query-local beta-min contract can separate statistical recoverability from post-selection thresholding while targeting only the graph and encoder class indexed by observed intervention labels.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a permutation-equivariant transcript-local certificate and, on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band, a strict all-dimension relaxation of the source's equation (22) premise while retaining its printed equation (23) threshold condition and every non-margin side condition. The reciprocal quantity \(\rho_i(G)\) is reported separately as a valid lower bound, not imposed as a new class assumption. Certified polynomial-bit spectral composition remains the first-class open question.

related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the sole strict finite-sample sufficient-condition comparator. Section 5 of the NeurIPS proceedings paper defines \(\eta^{\ast}\) in equation (22) as the minimum positive eigenvalue over all subset sums and prints \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\) in equation (23); Theorem 1 chooses thresholds strictly below those two quantities under Assumption 1 and score-difference consistency. The printed \(\gamma^{\ast}\) is not the reciprocal projector lower bound \(\rho^{\ast}\). Accordingly, Theorem 3 proves strict relaxation only of the all-subset spectral requirement on the common subregion already satisfying the reached projector band, while retaining the printed equation (23) threshold condition, smooth full support, intervention, parent-ratio, and score-consistency requirements. The reciprocal \(\rho_i(G)\) is a derived lower bound for each witnessed nonzero comparison rather than an added class assumption. No containment of the uncorrected published premise is claimed. Varıcı et al. (2025) supply the population score-difference range program that defines the transcript and are used as identification machinery rather than a tightening target. Squires et al. (2023) establish population linear causal disentanglement under one perfect intervention per node and validate the legal Gaussian subclass. Howard et al. (2021) provide time-uniform concentration machinery used to make stopping honest. Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026) are adjacent context only: their unknown multi-node covariance model and subset reconstruction are not placed in a theorem-level inclusion relation with the present class. Uhler et al. (2013) establish cancellation geometry for observational partial correlations; the Gaussian separation theorem concerns score-correlation matrices reached by a latent-intervention transcript and makes no tightening claim against their result. The ICALP proceedings paper of Sobczyk (2025) is a summary; Corollary 4.5 in the April 27, 2025 arXiv full version, version 2, supplies a certified spectral-projector primitive for Open-ended Question 1. Dey et al. (2023) provide complementary bit-growth templates, but neither source gives the adaptive end-to-end bit theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem is an exact-real statistical statement. It guarantees distance to a unit-row population range class and parent support, not an invertible encoder, a unique eigenvector inside a repeated positive eigenspace, or a latent-coordinate error independent of \(\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). The printed equation (23) norm product does not itself control actual projector comparisons; the comparison theorem therefore holds the reached projector band fixed and relaxes only equation (22). The bit-complexity result remains open and may require sharper interval bounds for projector-product norms than black-box eigensolver accuracy alone.
honest_scope: Theorems 1, 2, and 3 are posed on the linear Gaussian perfect-intervention subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\) and target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed ambient encoder class; no labelled latent graph is asserted to be a functional of \(P\). Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026) are adjacent rather than a theorem-level comparator. Theorem 3 gives a strict fixed-margin relaxation of Acartürk et al.'s equation (22) requirement only on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band; it retains their printed equation (23) threshold condition and all non-margin side conditions. The valid reciprocal \(\rho_i(G)\) is derived by Proposition 1 and is not a new assumption. The theorem does not claim that the printed norm product lower-bounds projector comparisons or that the uncorrected published sufficient region is contained in the transcript-local class. The result is not a minimax lower bound or a claim that the source's qualitative premise fails. When uncertainty radii vanish, Proposition 2 reduces the certificate to the known population program. No claim is made that \(g_0\) and \(h_0\) are jointly necessary for every causal representation learner.

literature_map.baseline: Acartürk et al. (2024) turn the score-difference geometry of Varıcı et al. (2025) into finite-sample graph and encoder guarantees. Their graph theorem uses smooth full-support densities, one distinct intervention per node, Assumption 1, score-estimator consistency (15), equation (22)'s all-subset \(\eta^{\ast}\), and equation (23)'s printed minimum norm product \(\gamma^{\ast}\). The valid projector lower bound is instead the reciprocal quantity \(\rho_i\), uniformly \(\rho^{\ast}\). The strict comparison therefore replaces only the fixed all-subset \(\eta^{\ast}\) bound by reached-query eigen bands on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band; it does not assert containment of the uncorrected source premise or add \(\rho^{\ast}\) as a class assumption. Squires et al. (2023) establish population identification for linearly mixed linear models under one perfect intervention per node. Howard et al. (2021) supply time-uniform matrix and covariance concentration. Uhler et al. (2013) document cancellation geometry for observational partial correlations. Sobczyk's ICALP 2025 paper is a proceedings summary, while Corollary 4.5 of the April 27, 2025 arXiv full version, version 2, supplies the exact spectral-projector primitive relevant to the open bit-complexity question.
